title: THE GOD WHO SEES AND COMES DOWN

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Lord said, "I have indeed seen the misery of my people in Egypt. I have heard them crying out because of their slave drivers, and I am concerned about their suffering. So I have come down to rescue them from the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them up out of that land into a good and spacious land, a land flowing with milk and honey—the home of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites."" - Exodus 3:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Count the personal words. I have seen. I have heard. I am concerned. I have come down. This is not a distant deity managing the universe from a safe height. This is a God who moves toward suffering.

For four hundred years it must have looked as though God was doing nothing. Now He says plainly: I saw all of it.

That matters for us. God's timing often looks like absence. It is not. The delay was never indifference.

And notice the direction — I have come down. That is the great movement of the whole Bible. God comes down to Babel, comes down to Sinai, and finally comes down in Bethlehem, when the Word became flesh and lived among us (Jn 1:14). Christianity is not a story of people climbing up to God. It is the story of God coming down to us.

Whatever misery you are in today, the God who came down in Christ has seen it. He is not watching from a distance.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe God has actually seen my situation, or do I feel overlooked?
2. How does the coming down of Jesus change how I read God's silence?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You see, hear, and come down. Meet me in what I am carrying, and remind me I am not overlooked. Amen.
